CLINICAL DOCUMENTATION — NARRATIVE EMERGENCY OBSERVATION NOTE V1
Patient: Jennifer Garcia | MRN: PAT-60006 | DOB: 1975-09-14 | Gender: Female | Doc ID: NARRATIVE_0006
Encounter Date: 2025-03-13 | Discharge/Note Date: 2025-03-16 | Provider: Dr. Allison Cameron, MD
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PRESENTATION
Patient Jennifer Garcia was triaged in the emergency department following acute onset of lightheadedness and palpitations
earlier this morning. Initial hemodynamic parameters were reviewed and patient was placed on telemetry.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
The patient describes experiencing recurrent lightheadedness over the preceding 48 hours without syncope. Initial
emergency workup revealed that initial bun was measured at 13.6 mg/dL. Point-of-care laboratory screening additionally
noted alanine aminotransferase (alt) resulted at 27.6 U/L. Given these findings, the patient was transitioned to the Clinical
Decision Unit for 24-hour observation.
OBSERVATION UNIT CLINICAL COURSE
Throughout the observation unit stay, continuous telemetry showed normal sinus rhythm without pause or tachyarrhythmia.
The patient was administered Amlodipine at a dose of 2.5 mg orally once daily, which promptly alleviated acute symptoms.
Follow-up protocol monitoring of sodium demonstrated 149.8 mmol/L (HIGH). Orthostatic blood pressures were negative
upon ambulation.
DISCHARGE REGIMEN
Patient was deemed safe for outpatient discharge. The ongoing regimen includes Cephalexin 500 mg PO every 6 hours for
10 days as prescribed. Prescription counseling was performed by nursing prior to release.
PLAN & PRECAUTIONS
Resume normal daily activities as tolerated. Avoid strenuous exercise until cardiology follow-up in 1 to 2 weeks. Immediate
emergency precautions detailed.
